scenario: Interpolating a binding introduced AFTER a mid-LHS negation must resolve, not silently drop the action. Rule `r` joins A, a `no N` negation, then B; the log action interpolates `{b.v}` — a binding declared after the negation. The activation token holds only the positive facts [A, B] (the negated N contributes none), so b is at token position 1. A lowering that uses the raw source pattern index (2) reads out of range and drops the interpolated log message.
rules_ds:
schema A scope logical:
    x: String key
schema N scope logical:
    x: String key
schema B scope logical:
    x: String key
    v: String mutable
rule r:
    A a
    no N n where n.x == a.x
    B b where b.x == a.x
->
    log critical "joinedval:{b.v}"
